study type: Descriptive cohort study and literature review
exposure: SMAD4 pathogenic missense variants (especially codon 500 variant and p.(Arg496Cys) variant)
outcome: Clinical phenotype (neurocognitive development, craniofacial features, short stature, pseudo-muscular build, hearing loss, thickened skin, joint limitations, cardiovascular manifestations, airway manifestations, fibrosis, scoliosis)
cohort: The participants were 24 adults with Myhre Syndrome (MS), including 17 diagnosed after the age of 18 years old.
finding: The study found that adults with Myhre Syndrome present with a milder phenotype and lower mortality rates compared to what is published in literature, with individuals having a codon 500 variant in SMAD4 showing a more pronounced neurodevelopmental and systemic phenotype, and new manifestations like scoliosis and fertility in males with the p.(Arg496Cys) variant were observed.
